overview: Two enzyme-detection tests that sort bacteria along completely different axes — one metabolic, one protective.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Detects cytochrome c oxidase, an enzyme in the electron transport chain of aerobic and some facultative organisms.
aspects.valueB: Detects catalase, an enzyme that breaks down hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.

aspects.label: Principle
aspects.valueA: A reagent (tetramethyl-p-phenylenediamine) turns dark purple/blue within seconds if oxidase is present.
aspects.valueB: Hydrogen peroxide added to growth produces visible gas bubbles if catalase is present.

aspects.label: Typical Use
aspects.valueA: Distinguishes oxidase-positive organisms like Pseudomonas and Neisseria from oxidase-negative Enterobacterales.
aspects.valueB: Distinguishes catalase-positive Staphylococcus/Micrococcus from catalase-negative Streptococcus/Enterococcus.

aspects.label: What It Reveals
aspects.valueA: Presence of an aerobic respiratory chain component — helps separate major Gram-negative bacterial groups.
aspects.valueB: Presence of an oxidative-stress defense enzyme — helps separate major Gram-positive coccal groups.

aspects.label: Procedure
aspects.valueA: Rub a colony onto reagent-impregnated filter paper or strip.
aspects.valueB: Add hydrogen peroxide directly to a colony on a slide or in a tube.

aspects.label: Clinical Example Use
aspects.valueA: Oxidase-positive Pseudomonas aeruginosa vs oxidase-negative Klebsiella pneumoniae.
aspects.valueB: Catalase-positive Staphylococcus aureus vs catalase-negative Streptococcus pyogenes.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Detects an aerobic respiratory enzyme, mainly used for Gram-negative rods.
aspects.valueB: Detects an oxidative-defense enzyme, mainly used for Gram-positive cocci.
